Why it's not an enum?

All existing code does it. I think there are two reasons:

- The LSP spec uses namespaces over enums. (Worth noting though that this is only the case for the specification which uses typescript types. A typescript enum cannot have a number associated with the value. In the [meta model](https://microsoft.github.io/language-server-protocol/specifications/lsp/3.17/metaModel/metaModel.json) (which AFAIK didn't exist when LSP was first implemented in Godot) those are called enums.)
- Also C++ enums can reference the value without the enum name. We don't want `lsp::Error` to be valid. (This could be solved using enum classes AFAIK, but I'm not sure whether they are approved for usage in Godot?)

Anyway, this might be worth a discussion but certainly not one to be had in a bugfix PR

I will change this, but it feels a bit inconsistent to me, that we don't allow declaring of multiple variables on one line, while enforcing three comparisons + one return value + one error message including string coercion on one line.
